title: Except “Thefts (ordinary)” which remained practically steady, and “Cheating” which showed an increase by 1.8%, all the offences against property, including such heinous crimes as “Dacoity”, “Robbery” and “House-breaking”, showed substantial decrease. As against this, there was an increase in all forms of crime against the person; “Murder” showing an increase by 0.5% “Kidnapping and Abduction” by 6.9%, “Riots” by 8.2% and miscellaneous offences against persons by 1.1%. This trend of increase in offences against persons was noticed last year also. The annual incidence of crime has also been worked out on the incidence of crime per 1,00,000 of population which is the accepted international standard, taking the population figures on the basis of the 1951 census

notes: The state of Assam registered the largest increase (9.2 per cent) followed by Kerala (6.5 per cent), Mysore (2.9 per cent), Madras (2.6 per cent) and Rajasthan (2.2 per cent) whereas noticeable decrease occurred in the states of Bihar (5.8 per cent), Bombay (5.3 per cent), Jammu and Kashmir (4.6 per cent) and Andhra Pradesh (4.1 per cent).

Amongst the cities, Kanpur registered the largest increase (15.4 per cent), followed by Hyderabad (7.8 per cent) and Bombay (2.5 per cent), whereas there was noticeable decrease in Bangalore (4.7 per cent) and Madras and Delhi (4.4 per cent each).

Amongst the Union Territories, Manipur and Tripura showed increase of 31.8% and 18.6% respectively. The high percentage of increase in these Territories is due to the comparatively low crime figures. A small increase in the total crime therefore gives a high percentage increase.

In Assam the high cost of essential commodities, activities of Naga hostiles in the districts of Sibsagar, United Mikir and North Cachar Hills as also import of a large number of labourers with unknown antecedents or work on the Brahmaputra Bridge Construction Project and installation of the oil refinery were held responsible for the increase. Madras attributed the increase to increased cost of living. Mysore ascribed the increase to adverse seasonal conditions in some parts of the State resulting in failure of crops, rise in prices of food grain, poor economic conditions and unemployment.
In Tripura, the increase was ascribed to the abnormal increase in the price of food stuffs and other essential commodities and depredations by raiders in the Indo-Pakistan border area.
